attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: It is a present-tense observation about the general state of accountability. In context, 'the companies' means the big GenAI firms Marcus is discussing (Microsoft, OpenAI, model trainers), and 'damage to society' means broad harms. The normalisation is acceptable but loses that context.

contract.note: The contract treats a generalisation as a universal negative covering any provider in any jurisdiction, so one isolated judgment would defeat it. In context, an ordinary reader would take the claim to be about major GenAI firms escaping broad accountability. A 10,000-yuan copyright award against a small Chinese operator does not fairly contradict that. The reading is stretched against the speaker.

evidence.note: A genuine Feb 2024 Guangzhou judgment holding a text-to-image operator liable for Ultraman copyright infringement. It concerns a small non-US provider and one individual copyright injury. It counts against only the contract's over-broad reading, not against the claim about the major companies.
Contemporary report that the Guangzhou judgment took effect before the post. It corroborates e1's status but has the same scope limits.
The Garante's notice to OpenAI states only alleged breaches, before any final decision. It is a regulator announcement mislabelled as a company disclosure, and it shows no liability was imposed.

reviews.rationale: The contract counts any single judgment against any provider worldwide as a contradiction, which stretches Marcus's general point about major GenAI firms. Under a fair reading, e1 and e2 are context only. e3 shows only allegations against OpenAI. The packet lacks comprehensive legal records showing whether major providers had escaped liability or a binding remedy by March 2024, so the claim cannot be settled on this evidence.
